[[File:Utsunomiya Shrine 08.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Main shrine building.]]

'''Utsunomiya Shrine''' (宇都宮神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Komaki|en|Komaki|qid=Q389537|lt=Komaki, Aichi|1=Komaki}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}. The shrine is notable for being the site of one of the largest {{ill|rectangular keyhole-shaped mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/rectangular keyhole-shaped mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in the Owari region, known as the '''Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun'''.

== History ==
* Late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|qid=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} to early {{ill|4th century|en|4th century|qid=Q8099|lt=4th century|1=4th century}} - built of the {{ill|rectangular keyhole-shaped mound|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/rectangular keyhole-shaped mound|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}.
* Around {{ill|1929|en|1929|qid=Q18792|lt=1929|1=1929}} (Showa 4) - Discovery of a {{ill|Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}}.
* [[September 9, 1987]] (Showa 62) - The kofun was Historic Site1 a [[Historic Site of Aichi Prefecture]], and the mirror was Historic Site1 a [[designation1 of Aichi Prefecture]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/yukei/kouko/kensitei/0733.html|title=Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror|publisher=Aichi Prefecture|accessdate=2013-05-22}}</ref>

== Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun ==
{{Infobox ancient site
| name = Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun
| location = 
| coordinates = {{coord|35|16|46.4|N|136|53|46.8|E|region:JP|display=inline}}

| map_size = Total length: 59m; height: approximately 6.5m; rear section: approximately 35m on each side

Located within the grounds of Utsunomiya Shrine, this is one of the largest {{ill|rectangular keyhole-shaped mounds|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/rectangular keyhole-shaped mounds|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in the Owari region. Part of the {{ill|Koki Kofun Cluster|ja|小木古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koki Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, it was constructed in the late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|qid=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} to early {{ill|4th century|en|4th century|qid=Q8099|lt=4th century|1=4th century}}. The presence of the kofun indicates the prominence of a powerful local clan during that era. In addition to this kofun, several others exist in the vicinity. The mound is 59m in total length, 6.5m in height, and approximately 35m on each side of the rear section. A vertical stone chamber is located within. The site was Historic Site1 a Historic Site of Aichi Prefecture in {{ill|1987|en|1987|qid=Q2429|lt=1987|1=1987}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/kinenbutu/siseki/kensitei/0923.html|title=Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun|publisher=Aichi Prefecture|accessdate=2013-05-22}}</ref>

== Historic Site ==
* Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror (三角縁獣文帯三神三獣鏡) - A {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|qid=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}} excavated from the Utsunomiya Shrine Kofun. It was discovered around {{ill|1929|en|1929|qid=Q18792|lt=1929|1=1929}} during the construction of the shrine hall at the front of the kofun and Historic Site1 a designation1 of Aichi Prefecture in {{ill|1987|en|1987|qid=Q2429|lt=1987|1=1987}}.

== location ==
{{ill|Komaki|en|Komaki|qid=Q389537|lt=Komaki, Aichi|1=Komaki}}, Ogi 3-chome 226.

== Access ==
* 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Ogi bus stop|ja|小木バス停留所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogi bus stop|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} served by {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|qid=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}}.
